name: App shortcuts
plain: Adds quick actions to the app icon's long press or right click menu.
meaning: Offers up to a few deep links from the OS launcher.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Adds quick actions to the app icon's long press or right click menu.

limits.headline: Can add quick actions to an installed app icon's long press or right click menu
limits.user_action: You install the app, then press and hold or right click its icon
can: Show a few links like Compose or New tab on the icon menu
Jump straight into part of the app
Use up to a handful of shortcuts
cannot: Add many shortcuts, since the system limits them
Work for a site that is not installed
Work in Firefox, or on iPhone Chrome
Open anything without you tapping the shortcut
limits.reach_label: A few shortcuts on one icon
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge, Samsung Internet and Safari on Mac support it. iPhone and Firefox do not.

story.what_it_is: An installed web app can add quick actions to its icon, like New message or Search.

marketing.name: App shortcuts
marketing.pitch: Lets an installed web app add quick actions to its icon's menu, as native apps do.

story.for_you: You press and hold the app icon, or right click it, and see quick actions like New post or Scan. One tap jumps you straight to that part of the app.
story.for_makers: Makers shorten the path to their main features, which raises use. It makes a web app feel as polished as a native one. It only works once the app is installed.

use_cases.example: Long press a social app icon and choose New post to open the compose screen.
A web mail icon offers Compose, so you start a draft in one tap.
A web music icon offers Liked songs and Search.
A web game launcher icon offers Continue game and Friends.
A store icon offers Track order and Cart.
A task app offers Add task, which opens a blank task.
A travel icon offers My trips and Boarding pass.
